FreeAgent Sole Trader Guide: MTD, Tax Returns & Why an Accountant Still Matters

FreeAgent is brilliant software - but if you're a sole trader using it without an accountant, there's a good chance your tax return has at least one costly mistake in it. That's not a criticism of the software. It's a reflection of how easy it is to get the setup wrong when you're working alone, without anyone checking your figures before they reach HMRC.

If you're a sole trader juggling invoices, tax deadlines, and Making Tax Digital on your own, you already know the admin never really stops. This guide will show you exactly how FreeAgent works, what it genuinely can't do for you alone, and three specific ways an accountant working alongside your FreeAgent account saves you more than their monthly fee. Specifically, you'll learn: what FreeAgent does brilliantly for self-employed people, the five mistakes sole traders make inside FreeAgent that only an accountant catches, and how MTD for Income Tax changes everything from April 2026 onwards.

If you're already wondering whether a combined software-plus-accountant approach makes sense, take a look at our sole trader accountancy packages with FreeAgent included - but first, let's make sure you understand exactly what you're working with.

What is FreeAgent and why is it built for sole traders?

FreeAgent is UK-built cloud accounting software launched in 2007 and acquired by RBS (now NatWest Group) in 2018. Unlike Xero or QuickBooks, which were designed to scale across business sizes and sectors, FreeAgent was built from the ground up for freelancers, contractors, sole traders, and small limited company directors. That focus shows in every part of the product.

The software connects directly to your business bank account, categorises transactions automatically, tracks your income and expenses in real time, and gives you a running estimate of your Self Assessment tax liability throughout the year. For a sole trader who previously kept records in a spreadsheet or a shoebox, this alone is transformative.

One reason FreeAgent has become so widely used among self-employed people in the UK is the free access route. If you hold a business account with NatWest, RBS, or Mettle, you get the full FreeAgent product at no additional cost. For sole traders who are already banking with one of those providers, the software question is effectively answered before any comparison with Xero or QuickBooks begins.

FreeAgent is also fully Making Tax Digital compliant, which matters enormously for sole traders right now. More on that shortly.

What FreeAgent actually does for you as a sole trader (and what it doesn't)

FreeAgent handles the daily mechanics of running a self-employed business well. You can raise and send invoices, record expenses, photograph receipts using FreeAgent Smart Capture, monitor your cashflow, and view a profit and loss summary at any point in the year. The tax timeline feature shows your estimated Self Assessment liability updating in real time as you add income and expenses - which removes the anxiety of a surprise tax bill in January.

For sole traders approaching or already past the VAT threshold, FreeAgent also manages VAT returns and submits them directly to HMRC. The software handles the MTD for VAT submission process automatically once it's set up correctly.

What FreeAgent doesn't do is think. It records what you tell it to record. It categorises transactions based on rules you set or approve. It cannot tell you whether you've categorised something incorrectly, whether your year-end date is set up properly, or whether you're claiming all the allowable expenses you're entitled to. It won't flag that you've entered your drawings as a salary expense - one of the most common and costly mistakes sole traders make. And it certainly won't advise you on how to structure your income to minimise your tax bill legally.

The software is the tool. The accountant is the expert who makes it work properly. That distinction matters more than most sole traders realise until something goes wrong.

FreeAgent and Making Tax Digital: what every sole trader needs to know in 2026

Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD for ITSA) is the most significant change to Self Assessment in a generation. From April 2026, sole traders and landlords with qualifying annual income over £50,000 must submit quarterly updates to HMRC digitally, using MTD-compatible software. From April 2027, that threshold drops to £30,000. From April 2028, it drops further to £20,000. Our Making Tax Digital guide has the full dates, deadlines and penalties.

FreeAgent is MTD-compatible. You can generate and submit your quarterly updates directly to HMRC through the software. But compatible software and a correctly managed MTD process are two different things. The quarterly submissions must reflect accurate, categorised records. If your bookkeeping is behind, your categories are wrong, or your year-end settings are incorrect, your quarterly submissions will be wrong too - and HMRC will have four data points per year to notice the discrepancy, not one.

The GOV.UK guidance on MTD for Income Tax sets out the technical requirements, but it doesn't tell you how to manage the quarterly workflow in practice. That's where an accountant who works inside FreeAgent with you makes a concrete difference: reviewing your records each quarter before submission, catching errors before they reach HMRC, and ensuring your end-of-year declaration is accurate.

At Focus Accountancy, our Sole Trader MTD package includes quarterly FreeAgent reviews specifically for this reason. We check your records, confirm your categorisations, and submit your quarterly updates - so you're not doing this alone four times a year.

The five most common FreeAgent mistakes sole traders make without an accountant

We've seen these errors repeatedly at Focus Accountancy, and every one of them has a real cost - either in overpaid tax, underpaid tax that triggers an HMRC investigation, or both.

1. Entering drawings as a salary expense. As a sole trader, the money you take from your business is not a wage. It's drawings, and it appears after profit on your profit and loss statement. Entering it as a salary expense reduces your reported profit artificially, which means you're under-declaring your taxable income. HMRC can investigate years of returns if this is discovered, and the resulting tax bill plus penalties can be severe.

2. Setting the wrong year-end date. FreeAgent needs to be configured with the right accounting year end, which for most sole traders now means 5 April or 31 March (HMRC treats the two as the same under the tax-year basis). If this is set incorrectly, your tax calculations will be based on the wrong period. We've seen sole traders submit multiple years of returns with this error in place, resulting in both over and under-declarations of tax.

3. Miscategorising expenses. FreeAgent gives you categories to choose from, but it doesn't know your business. A sole trader IT consultant categorising client entertainment as a general business expense, or missing the distinction between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure, will produce a tax return that doesn't reflect their actual position. Some of these errors result in paying more tax than necessary; others create compliance risk.

4. Missing allowable expenses entirely. FreeAgent records what you put in. It won't prompt you to claim use-of-home expenses, mileage at the approved HMRC rate, professional subscriptions, or training costs relevant to your trade. Sole traders working without an accountant routinely leave hundreds or thousands of pounds of legitimate deductions unclaimed every year.

5. Ignoring the VAT threshold. FreeAgent doesn't automatically alert you when your rolling 12-month turnover approaches the £90,000 VAT registration threshold. [CONFIRM: check FreeAgent has no VAT threshold alert] If you cross it without registering, you become liable for VAT on all your sales from the date you should have registered - not from the date you actually did. The penalties for late registration can be significant.

Do you still need an accountant if you use FreeAgent? (Honest answer)

Yes. And the reason is specific, not vague.

FreeAgent is excellent at recording and reporting. It is not capable of advising, reviewing, or catching errors in its own data. An accountant working alongside your FreeAgent account does three things the software cannot: they review your records for accuracy before anything reaches HMRC, they advise you on tax planning decisions that reduce your liability legally, and they take responsibility for your compliance - so if HMRC has a question, you have a professional in your corner.

The question most sole traders are really asking is whether the cost of an accountant is justified when they already have software. In our experience, the answer is almost always yes - because the tax savings from correctly claimed expenses and proper planning typically exceed the accountancy fee.

Christian, one of our clients, put it well: "Helpful, knowledgeable team that make time to provide jargon-free planning and advice." That's exactly what FreeAgent can't give you - a knowledgeable professional who understands your specific situation and explains it without jargon.

Another client who moved to us from a previous accountant told us: "I have felt like a valued client and the move to Focus Accountancy was definitely the right one for my business." The combination of FreeAgent's real-time visibility and an accountant's professional oversight is genuinely more powerful than either alone.

To understand more about how we work with FreeAgent as a FreeAgent Gold Partner, read about our FreeAgent partnership and what it means for you.

Does FreeAgent do Self Assessment tax returns for sole traders?

FreeAgent can prepare and file your Self Assessment tax return directly with HMRC, pulling your income and expense data from the records you've maintained throughout the year. However, the accuracy of that return depends entirely on the accuracy of your bookkeeping. An accountant reviews the return before it's filed, checks for missed allowances and confirms the figures are correct - which is something the software itself cannot do.

What you get when FreeAgent is included in your accountancy package

When FreeAgent is bundled into an accountancy package rather than used as a standalone tool, the dynamic changes completely. You're not just getting software - you're getting a professional who works inside that software with you, sees the same data you see, and intervenes before errors become problems.

At Focus Accountancy, every sole trader package includes a FreeAgent subscription as standard. Our entry-level Sole Trader package covers your tax return, annual review meeting, and unlimited phone and email support. Our Sole Trader MTD package adds quarterly FreeAgent reviews and Making Tax Digital submissions - which is the package most sole traders with turnover over £30,000 will need from April 2027 as MTD thresholds drop.

For sole traders who want their bookkeeping handled entirely, our Sole Trader MTD with Bookkeeping package includes FreeAgent Smart Capture and a full bookkeeping service, so you're not categorising transactions yourself at all. You focus on your work; we handle the numbers.

How Focus Accountancy's sole trader packages work with FreeAgent included

We're a Bristol-based accountancy firm ranked among the top UK accountants, and we've built our sole trader packages specifically around the way self-employed people actually work. That means affordable monthly packages, unlimited email and telephone support, and FreeAgent included as standard - not as an add-on.

The process is simple. When you join, we set up your FreeAgent account correctly from the start: the right year-end date, the right VAT settings if applicable, and the right expense categories for your trade. We show you how to connect your bank feed, configure Smart Capture if you're on the bookkeeping package, and make sure your MTD settings are in place before the quarterly submission deadlines arrive.

From there, we're available by phone and email whenever you have a question - whether that's about categorising an unusual expense, understanding a tax notice from HMRC, or planning ahead for a higher-income year. Our quarterly reviews mean we're looking at your FreeAgent data four times a year, not just at year end. And our annual review meeting gives you a clear picture of your tax position, your allowances, and any planning opportunities for the year ahead.

The focus is always on you. We handle the accounting and finance part so you can focus on the work that actually earns your income. If you'd like to understand which package fits your situation, we offer a free, no-obligation 30-minute video call to provide a personalised quote - no pressure, just a clear conversation about what you need.

To find out more about the team behind the service, meet the Focus Accountancy team and see how we work.

Ready to stop using FreeAgent alone and start using it properly? Explore our sole trader accountancy packages with FreeAgent included and book your free consultation today.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can sole traders use FreeAgent for free?

Sole traders who hold a business account with NatWest, RBS, or Mettle can access the full FreeAgent product at no additional cost as part of their banking relationship. For sole traders who bank elsewhere, FreeAgent is available on a paid subscription. Many accountancy firms, including Focus Accountancy, include a FreeAgent subscription within their monthly packages, which means you get the software and professional oversight for a single combined fee rather than paying for both separately.

What is the difference between FreeAgent for sole traders and limited companies?

FreeAgent offers different account configurations for sole traders and limited companies, reflecting the different tax and reporting requirements of each structure. Sole trader accounts are set up around Self Assessment, profit and loss reporting, and MTD for Income Tax submissions. Limited company accounts include additional features for corporation tax, payroll, dividends, and Companies House filing. The core interface is similar, but the underlying tax logic and reporting outputs are different - which is one reason why getting the initial setup right with an accountant matters, because the wrong configuration produces the wrong tax calculations from day one.

How much does FreeAgent cost for a sole trader in the UK?

FreeAgent is free for sole traders who bank with NatWest, RBS, or Mettle. For those who don't, FreeAgent charges a monthly subscription fee directly. However, many sole traders find that the most cost-effective route is an accountancy package that includes FreeAgent as standard, since this combines the software cost with professional tax and compliance support for a single monthly fee - removing the need to manage the software alone while also covering your Self Assessment return, MTD submissions, and ongoing advice.
